rationale: The customer said only 'funny smell' and the assistant immediately fired a stop-use card framed around 'a burning or hot-plastic smell' without asking what the smell was like or where it came from, which is the sensible first step per ground truth (a funny oven smell is often fat burn-off). By luck the hidden truth was an electrical hazard, so the stop-use, switch-off-at-fuse-box and no-further-use advice is correct and safe, but it is uncalibrated and skipped all diagnostic work, never surfacing the scorched warm cooker switch, flicker or crackle, and did not point to an electrician for the supply/switch. No fabrication is stated as fact, no parts, no loop, but a UK homeowner is left with a blunt, context-free escalation.
